articleTitle: High accuracy, 150 dB, attenuation measurement system for traceability at radio frequencies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: The author describes the series audio frequency (AF) substitution attenuator calibrator which was designed and made at NPL, Malvern in 1988. It was designed to cover the range 0.5-50 MHz and, later on, the upper limit was extended to 100 MHz. The two synthesized sources employed are always operated 10 kHz apart and they are both locked to the same ultra-stable 10 MHz crystal-controlled oscillator; after mixing, an extremely stable 10 kHz intermediate frequency is always produced. The attenuation reference standard is a seven decade precision inductive voltage divider (IVD), which is inserted between two 10 kHz tuned amplifiers. At each setting of the device under test (DUT), the IVD and, if necessary, the gauge block attenuator (GBA) are adjusted so that the output voltage returns to the same value.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Untuned systems for the calibration of electrical noise sources
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: The design of untuned radiometers is demonstrated. The resulting systems allow for broader band operation. The coaxial system described is more amenable to multi-frequency operation under computer control, and in principle can measure at any frequency within the 10 MHz to 18 GHz band. Computer controlled multi-frequency operation of the mm-wave systems is limited by the unavailability of suitable tuneable band-pass filters. However, investigations are proceeding in an attempt to exploit some of the recent developments in the quasi-optical field.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Model fitting of millimetre wave photodiodes to scalar optical and vector return-loss measurements
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: The microwave characteristics of a photo detector diode are derived from scalar optoelectronic and microwave vector return-loss measurements. A computer program is used to devise an equivalent circuit to match the measured microwave frequency response. The diode equivalent circuit gives a good match to the measured performance and calculates previously undetermined phase response information.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Vector measurements using a scalar analyser and diode detectors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: The capability of a scalar network analyser with diode detectors has been extended by the addition of some waveguide hardware to provide vector measurements over the frequency range 26.5 to 40 GHz. Two methods are described to compensate for the non-linear response of the diode detectors and a comparison of measurements with a thermistor-based multistate reflectometer shows that comparable measurements can be obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Oscillator noise measurements at millimetre wave-lengths
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: To achieve the high sensitivity with FM noise measurements, a key requirement is to have a low loss frequency discriminator with as large a discriminator slope as possible. The measurement technique used in this system uses a very high Q quasi-optical cavity in reflection which gives an extremely high discriminator slope. Typical values for the loaded Q are in excess of 100000 with almost zero insertion loss, which is over an order of magnitude better than that previously achieved with waveguide cavities. (An increase in Q by a factor of 10 can be expected to decrease the noise floor by a factor of 20 dB). Compared to delay line techniques at this frequency, the improvement in sensitivity can be better than 40 dB. This technique allows very high sensitivity at low input power over an ultra wideband frequency range.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The measurement of mismatched noise sources without isolators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: A simple correction for mismatch only applies when the noise contribution from a receiver is the same for all noise sources. But amplifier noise is affected by the match it 'sees' at its input; hence the requirement for isolators to be inserted between source and receiver to ensure constant receiver noise. Unfortunately, isolators are unavailable at low MHz frequencies. An alternative solution is considered which is based on characterising the receiver so that its noise contribution is known for any noise source impedance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of a broadband VHF six-port for high precision impedance measurements
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: The author summarizes work carried out on a VHF single six-port reflectometer to improve the measurement stability under normal laboratory conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multistate reflectometer in dielectric guide
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: An implementation of a four-port multistate reflectometer using dielectric guide for the frequency band 75-140 GHz is presented along with all its necessary components. The authors focus on the realisation of a phase shifter. The characteristics of the final instrument are measured at intermediate frequencies and a calibration performed at 94 GHz. Measurements were performed at the National Standards Division at RSRE in Great Malvern and subsequent results are in good agreement with theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Guidance on the use of coaxial connectors in radio frequency and microwave circuits
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: It is suggested that coaxial connectors are widely misused and their electrical and mechanical performance taken for granted. Coaxial connectors are often the most mistreated part of a measurement system. The author deals with the following topics associated with the use of coaxial connectors: connector repeatability; repeatability assessment; standard specifications for coaxial connectors; interface dimensions and gauging; and connector cleaning. It is recommended that all instruments fitted with connectors submitted for calibration should be adequately tested to ensure compliance to their mechanical specifications. All terminations mismatches, inter-series connectors and adaptors, etc., should also be tested. Calibration work should not be commenced if a connector is found to be outside the mechanical compliance limits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A millimetre wave power transfer technique
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'What's New in Microwave Measurements' (Digest No: 1990/174)
abstract: The techniques described involve the use of a multistate reflectometer. Calibration of the multistate is performed by attaching to the output port a series of short circuits and loads and the parameters of the calibration are found by processing the ratios of two power meters. Dealing in ratios, the system is effectively levelled and the quantity Gamma /sub g/, the effective reflection coefficient of the multistate reflectometer, is calculated as part of the calibration routine.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
